candidates.tagline: Batman's concept bike: deadly on the outside, deadlier if you actually tried to ride it
candidates.story: On October 22, 2026, HotCars analyzed an AI-generated Batman motorcycle concept by Instagram artist darkkuston; while it looks menacing, real riders immediately spot that the front wheel sits so close to the bodywork that any bump or hard braking would cause the tire to strike the cowl — catastrophic at speed.
candidates.why_funny: The Caped Crusader's imaginary engineers nailed the 'insane' brief but missed the part where the front wheel needs room to actually turn and absorb bumps.
candidates.alt: AI-rendered futuristic Batman motorcycle in matte black and yellow with massive tires, low handlebars, and an angular front cowl that sits dangerously close to the front wheel

candidates.tagline: Smart lock with no key. Except when the battery dies — then you crank it like a 1920s car
candidates.story: On October 7, 2026, Amazon Ring unveiled its first smart lock at $249 — fingerprint reader, touchscreen keypad, app control, no physical key — but added a knurled 'Power Dial' crank below the keypad so you can hand-generate enough power to unlock the door when the battery inevitably dies.
candidates.why_funny: Ring solved the 'what if our keyless smart lock loses power' problem by bolting on the oldest energy technology known to humans: a hand crank.
candidates.alt: The Ring Smart Lock mounted on a door: a sleek rectangular device with a circular fingerprint reader at top, a backlit touchscreen keypad in the middle, and a manual knurled dial crank at the bottom
